title: Two orders share a pool transition; each owner keeps a separate result

inputs.label: Shared pool before
lines: Price, fee and rounding rules not supplied

outputs.label: Owner one
lines: 92 B meets this order’s 90 B floor

outputs.label: Owner two
lines: 92 B meets this order’s 90 B floor

outputs.label: Shared pool continuation
lines: Closing reserves cannot be calculated from supplied facts

checks.label: Each owner’s minimum
checks.explanation: Each owner gives 100 A and receives 92 B net against their own minimum of 90 B. The 2 B above the floor is not an identified fee.

checks.label: One shared pool update
checks.explanation: A complete pool relation must explain the same two orders under its reserve, fee and exact-rounding rules. This illustration supplies no pool calculation.

checks.label: Allocate each payment once
checks.explanation: The consuming validator checks actual output allocation. This illustration uses a separate output for each order; the two owner receipts cannot be counted as the same payment.

note: PROPOSED worked example, not an executed batch. Show two order-to-owner lanes coupled to a shared pool continuation. The owner-side totals are 200 A given and 184 B received; they do not specify a complete pool ledger. Check count does not determine Strand count.

title: Issue 300 units, distribute all 300, retain 700 units of capacity

outputs.label: Capacity left under the cap
lines: Unissued capacity; no asset payment or debt

checks.label: Continue supply within the cap
checks.explanation: The proposed first issue is 300 ≤ 1,000. The application asset’s own minting policy must enforce the actual supply change and continue the supply state.

checks.label: Reconcile mint and recipient outputs
checks.explanation: The two recipient amounts sum to the proposed new supply: 180 + 120 = 300. The policy and consumer must check the actual mint and recipient outputs.

checks.label: Separate supply from servicing promises
checks.explanation: The 700 units of capacity are not debt. A redemption duty exists only if the program defines its parties, asset, creation and discharge rules; none is supplied here.

note: PROPOSED application accounting, not an executed mint or datum schema. Draw a 300-unit issue branching into the 180/120 recipient payments, beside a supply-capacity continuation. The supply and capacity annotations are not additional asset outputs. Web proof-claim issuance does not mint the application asset.

title: Debt changes by 35 CASH while the payer spends 37 CASH

inputs.label: Period accrual premise
lines: Rate, period and rounding not supplied

checks.label: Add the supplied accrual
checks.explanation: Opening debt 100 CASH plus the illustrative 5 CASH accrual gives a 105 CASH duty before payment. The example does not derive 5 CASH from a rate schedule.

checks.label: Pay the lender and fee recipient separately
checks.explanation: The payer’s gross debit is 37 CASH, consisting of a 35 CASH repayment and a 2 CASH fee. Actual parties, exact CASH identity and outputs must match the payer’s intent.

checks.label: Carry the debt that remains
checks.explanation: Only the 35 CASH repayment discharges debt, leaving 70 CASH. The fee is not repayment. No principal/interest allocation or collateral release is specified.

note: PROPOSED servicing arithmetic, not an executed loan or datum schema. Use an obligation line 100 → 105 → 70 above a cash fork 37 → lender 35 + fee recipient 2. A connector from repayment 35 to debt discharge should show why the fee does not reduce debt.

title: An allocation pays 23 A and 4 B, retaining backing for two duties

inputs.label: Opening custody premise
lines: Source step needs at least 23 A and 4 B for non-negative custody

checks.label: Check approval and division inputs
checks.explanation: Source allocate requires approved and not allocated, remainder < 3, units = 3 × quotient + remainder, units ≥ 3 and nonzero quotient. approved=false fails the source precondition. No distinct governance approver is supplied.

checks.label: Derive and reconcile actual transfers
checks.explanation: Alpha receives quotient × 2 = 14 A and fixed 4 B; beta receives quotient = 7 A; the fee is fixed 2 A. Custody debit is 23 A and 4 B. The units parameter is not another debit.

checks.label: Continue custody and duties asset by asset
checks.explanation: The proposed opening leaves 2 A and 6 B, matching reserve duty 2 A and rebate duty 6 B. Full backing is an additional application policy. rebate(amount) can discharge B rebate; S13 has no allocation-reserve discharge action.

note: Source arithmetic with a PROPOSED backing premise, not an executed treasury transaction. Use separate A and B custody rows branching to beneficiaries/fees, then align retained A/B with matching duty rows. Duties record amounts owed; they are not extra outgoing payments. Approval consent and a separate governance decision are distinct in the attributed source reading.
